title: Common accessibility rank for a small family of presentable infinity categories and functors
statement: Let $I$ be a small infinity category, let $(\mathcal C_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of presentable infinity categories indexed by the objects of $I$, and let $(T_e:\mathcal C_{s(e)}\to\mathcal C_{t(e)})$ be a family of coherent functors indexed by the arrows $e:s(e)\to t(e)$ of $I$, each accessible, meaning that $T_e$ preserves small $\rho_e$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular cardinal $\rho_e\in\mathcal U$. Then there is an uncountable regular cardinal $\lambda\in\mathcal U$ such that every $\mathcal C_i$ is $\lambda$-accessible and every $T_e$ preserves small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. The universes, filteredness and accessibility used here are those of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent infinity categories and functors are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.4.2.9 (a kappa-accessible infinity category is kappa'-accessible whenever kappa << kappa'), Definition A.2.6.3 and the note after it (arbitrarily large kappa' with kappa << kappa'), and Remark 5.4.2.13 (simultaneous enlargement of the rank of the categories and functors)

proof.text: For each vertex $i$ choose an infinite regular $\kappa_i\in\mathcal U$ witnessing accessibility of $\mathcal C_i$, using presentability. For each edge $e$ choose the infinite regular $\rho_e\in\mathcal U$ from the hypothesis. The vertex set $I_0$ and edge set $I_1$ are small because $I$ is a small simplicial set. Apply [lem-coef-small-family-regular-bound] to the small family of sets consisting of an ordinal representative of each $\kappa_i$, an ordinal representative of each $\rho_e$, and a copy of $\mathbb N$. Obtain an infinite regular cardinal $\theta\in\mathcal U$ strictly greater than the cardinality of their disjoint union. Each summand injects into that union, so $\kappa_i<\theta$, $\rho_e<\theta$, and $\aleph_0<\theta$. Including the last summand also handles the empty indexing category.

source.place: Definition 5.5.0.1; the small-family bound is an agent-explicit set-theoretic preparation for Definition A.2.6.3. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text:
Put $\sigma=2^	heta$ and let $\lambda=\sigma^+$ be its successor cardinal. The power set and successor remain in $\mathcal U$. By [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-square-power], $	heta<\sigma$ and $\sigma^	heta=\sigma$; by [lem-coef-infinite-cardinal-successor-regular], $\lambda$ is infinite regular. Thus $\lambda$ is uncountable. If $\mu<\lambda$ and $
u<\kappa_i$, then $\mu\leq\sigma$ by the definition of successor, and $
u\leq	heta$. Choose sets $M,N,S,T$ of cardinalities $\mu,
u,\sigma,	heta$, injections $a:M\hookrightarrow S$ and $b:N\hookrightarrow T$, and a point $s_0\in S$ (which exists since $\sigma$ is infinite). Send $f:N	o M$ to the function $g:T	o S$ given by $g(b(n))=a(f(n))$ and $g(t)=s_0$ outside $b(N)$. Restricting to $b(N)$ and using injectivity of $a$ recovers $f$, so this is an injection even when $M$ or $N$ is empty. Hence $\mu^
u\leq\sigma^	heta=\sigma<\lambda$. This verifies the sharp power bound simultaneously for all $i$, without assuming that the original $\kappa_i$ have a common accessibility rank before enlargement.

source.place: Definition A.2.6.3 and the immediately following successor-cardinal example; the common choice is agent-explicit. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $i$. The cardinals $\kappa_i<\lambda$ are infinite regular in $\mathcal U$, $\mathcal C_i$ is $\kappa_i$-accessible by step 1, and step 2 gives $\mu^\nu<\lambda$ for every $\mu<\lambda$ and $\nu<\kappa_i$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-sharp-accessibility-enlargement] with its lower cardinal equal to $\kappa_i$ and its upper cardinal equal to $\lambda$. It follows that every $\mathcal C_i$ is $\lambda$-accessible.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9 Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Fix an edge $e$ and a small $\lambda$-filtered quasicategory $J$. Every $\rho_e$-small simplicial set is $\lambda$-small because $\rho_e<\theta<\lambda$. Consequently every coherent diagram from a $\rho_e$-small simplicial set into $J$ has a cocone by $\lambda$-filteredness; thus $J$ is $\rho_e$-filtered, including the empty test diagram. Given a diagram $F:J\to\mathcal C_{s(e)}$ and any colimiting cocone on it, the preservation hypothesis for $T_e$ applies and says precisely that its image is colimiting in $\mathcal C_{t(e)}$. These colimits exist since the source category is presentable. Hence $T_e$ preserves all small $\lambda$-filtered colimits. This reasoning applies to every edge, and uses none of the coherence data to change the specified functors, proving the remaining conclusion.

source.place: Definition 5.3.1.7 and Definition 5.4.2.5, parenthetical monotonicity observation Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof_origin.place: Agent-explicit simultaneous cardinal argument from Definition A.2.6.3 and Proposition 5.4.2.9, read online; no archived HTT copy is present. Functor monotonicity is written directly from filteredness.
